title: MCP Auth in Production — Enrollment, JWKS Refresh, Audience-Pinned Tokens

questions.question: A service validates access tokens with signing keys it downloaded once at startup. Months later every request suddenly fails after the identity provider rotates its keys. What was missing?
options: A longer token lifetime so rotation never matters
Harder key names that are difficult to guess
A weekly service restart on a fixed schedule
Scheduled refresh of the cached keys before they expire, plus a fetch on cache miss
questions.explanation: Keys rotate on someone else's schedule, so validation needs a cache with refresh and a fallback fetch. This lesson builds the production auth surface around that rule.

questions.question: What does valid dynamic client registration return?
options: 200 with the plaintext registration secret only
404 because DCR is disabled
403 until the first token exchange
201 plus metadata and a hashed registration token
questions.explanation: A valid redirect URI and supported authentication method produce 201; the server stores only a hash of the returned registration token.

questions.question: What does ResourceServer.refresh_jwks do after an unknown key id?
options: Re-fetches the authorization server's published JWKS into its cache; it does not rotate signing keys
It signs a replacement token locally
It accepts any key whose id is new
It deletes all cached keys permanently
questions.explanation: The resource server re-fetches the authorization server's published JWKS into its cache; signing-key rotation remains an authorization-server operation.

questions.question: In what order does validate reject a token with an untrusted issuer?
options: It first tries the tool backend and then checks issuer
401 iss not allowed before JWKS work
It returns 403 missing scope
It accepts the token if its audience is correct
questions.explanation: Issuer allowlisting is an early authentication check, so the resource server returns 401 before spending work on key lookup or scope authorization.

questions.question: What happens when a valid notes token is replayed to the tasks resource?
options: It succeeds because both resources use the same issuer
It is downgraded to read-only
It returns 401 for an audience mismatch
It returns 403 only if the task is complete
questions.explanation: The token's aud is pinned to the notes resource; using it at another resource server fails authentication with audience mismatch.

questions.question: What scope must the elevated token carry for the demonstrated notes.delete operation?
options: No scope because delete is local
Only mcp:tools.invoke
Only the registration token
mcp:tools.delete in addition to mcp:tools.invoke
questions.explanation: TOOL_SCOPES maps notes.delete to mcp:tools.delete; the demo issues an elevated token containing that scope plus the ordinary invoke scope.
